import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I found the cause, wrote a plan for the fix, and submitted it for your approval. No code has been changed yet.

**Cause:** the code that builds the `I` (Block ID) row hard-codes the caret: `value = \`^${blockId}\``. That value is used for both what the row shows and what gets copied, so both include the `^`. The line is in `plugins/bob-navigation-hotkeys/src/101-copy-card-model.js` in the bob-plugins repo. The block ID itself is already stored without the caret, and so is the `{block_id}` template variable.

**The plan** (a single-agent plan, sized `small`):
1. **Fix the row:** the `I` row copies `bank-records` instead of `^bank-records`. What the row shows, what lands on the clipboard and the `Copied …` notice all match. Rows with no block ID behave as they do now.
2. **Templates stay the same:** a template like `the ^{block_id} task in the {path} file` still produces exactly one `^`. The existing tests for your Task ref template are kept to guard this.
3. **Tests:** update the expected values in the unit tests and the real-Obsidian end-to-end harness, and add a check that the row's display matches what it copies.
4. **Docs:** update the `I` row and the `yank-block-id` description in `docs/copy-card.md`, and add one line saying a `^{block_id}` template gives you the caret version if you ever want it.
5. **Release:** rebuild the plugin, bump its version from `2.81.0` to `2.81.1`, run the full test and docs checks, run the real-Obsidian end-to-end test, and deploy with `bob plugins sync`. If Obsidian can't launch on this machine, the agent will say so rather than claim that test passed.

**Decision for you (`yank_command`):** should the `yank-block-id` command (command palette, no hotkey) also copy the ID without the `^`? It has its own copy of the same `^` code.
- **`bare` (default):** yes, so both ways of copying a block ID give the same result.
- **`caret`:** only the `I` row changes; `yank-block-id` keeps copying `^id`.

The agent that does the work starts once you approve the plan.
